facts.text: I have pain on the right side of my chest.

facts.item: chest pain: worse when breathing in
facts.text: It gets worse when I breathe in.

facts.item: when the fever, chills and headache started
facts.text: The fever, chills and headache started three days after my gallbladder operation.
I'm bringing up phlegm when I cough.
I've had it for the last 12 hours.
Three days ago I had an open operation to take out my gallbladder. The cut is below my right ribs.
I had a hysterectomy through my abdomen 16 years ago.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions.
I don't take any regular medications.
I smoke a pack of cigarettes a day, and have for 17 years.
I haven't noticed any problems with my heart.

facts.item: belly symptoms apart from the surgery
facts.text: Apart from the surgery cut, my belly has been fine.
I haven't had any problems with my muscles or joints.

f012: Source: 'Chronic_Conditions: None reported'; read as a denial per the meta-phrase rule.
f013: Source: 'Medications: None reported'; read as no regular medications. Peri-operative medicines after the cholecystectomy are not documented.
f015: From the ROS line 'Cardiovascular: No reported abnormalities'. The right-sided pleuritic chest pain is the chief complaint and is filed as respiratory; this denial covers other heart symptoms.

x005: 'Appears uncomfortable' is a general-appearance observation filed under respiratory inspection in the source; kept in the lung examination record.

source_issues: ROS 'Neurological: No reported abnormalities' contradicts the reported headache; the neurological denial is not encoded.
ROS 'Cardiovascular: No reported abnormalities' sits next to a chief complaint of chest pain (pleuritic, so plausibly not cardiac).
Respiratory percussion and palpation, and abdominal auscultation and percussion, are 'Not specified'.
Alcohol use, occupation and activities are 'Not specified'.
The demographics describe the patient as obese; no other field mentions it.
notes: The chest pain appears only in the chief complaint; its location (right side) is in the parent text and 'increases on inspiration' is a child. The pain is filed under the respiratory system because it is pleuritic.

Surgery three days ago (p006) and symptom onset three days after surgery (p001) are consistent: the fever, chills and headache began on about post-operative day 3. The onset applies to three symptoms, so it is a standalone fact (f006).
The productive cough appears in p002 and p008; one cough fact with 'productive' and '12 hours' as children.

'None reported' and 'No reported abnormalities' are treated as denials where they carry that meaning (chronic conditions, medications, cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal apart from the surgical site). 'Not specified' social-history items are left unknown, with no facts.
Obesity (from the demographics) is in qc.extras.acting_notes as a visible characteristic, not a patient fact.

extras.objective_for_doctor: Evaluate the patient presenting with postoperative fever, chest pain that increases on inspiration, and a productive cough, and determine the correct diagnosis.
